name: Find clients who stopped coming
description: Someone who HAS been a client — that is the whole difference between this and the enquiry follow-up, and it is what makes the message honest: there is a real relationship to refer back to. Quiet is tested TWICE, by the appointment hour and by when the booking was made, and the second is not belt-and-braces. A booking for a non-scheduled service — a course, a package, anything not an hour in the diary — carries NO `start_time` at all, so the hour test alone reads it as ancient. On this account that put a client who had bought something nine days earlier on the lapsed list. Both hops are `none`, so one recent booking of either kind is enough to leave somebody alone, which also covers the client already rebooked for next week: telling them you have missed them reads as a business that does not know who is coming. THE UPPER BOUND IS THE OWNER'S, not mine: `{{input.stop_after_days}}` arrives as a negative offset from `agent_config`, chosen on the install dialog. It was a number written into this file, which meant every business on the platform gave up at the same moment regardless of what they sell. For this agent it is a FLOOR as well as a bound: somebody whose last booking predates it has left, and a warm note about coming back reads as a cold mailshot.

name: Write to each one personally
description: Ten at a time, and fewer than the enquiry agent sends on purpose: this is the one list in the product where the recipient did not ask to hear from us recently, and a monthly batch of ten reads as a business thinking of someone. Thirty reads as a mailshot. ONE PERSON'S REFUSAL MUST NOT STOP THE REST. In production a failing scatter item re-throws and aborts the whole run unless `continueOnError` is set, and per-person refusals are ordinary here: somebody unsubscribed since the last run, an address that bounces, a transport error. Worst of all, the find is ordered OLDEST FIRST, so the one person who cannot be written to would sit at the top of the list and block everybody behind them on every run, for good. The gather phase already separates the failures from the sends, so the run reports honestly instead of stopping.

steps.name: Write the opening line
steps.description: ONE sentence into the template's `personalLine` slot. The booking link, subject, greeting, language and sign-off all belong to `booking-invite` — the same template the enquiry chaser has used since it shipped.
steps.prompt:
Write ONE short opening sentence for an email from a small business owner to a PAST CLIENT who has not booked anything in more than six months.

The person:
  name: {{current_contact.first_name}} {{current_contact.last_name}}
  how they first came to us: {{current_contact.source}}
  what we know about them: {{current_contact.notes}}

RULES, all of them absolute:
1. Write in the SAME LANGUAGE as the person's own words above. Never translate or transliterate their name.
2. ONE sentence. It sits at the top of an email that already has a greeting, a booking button and a sign-off — you are writing none of those.
3. Never write a link, a URL, a price, a date, a discount or a service name. The email supplies the booking link itself, and an offer you invented is one the owner never agreed to.
4. Never invent a fact about what they had done, when they last came, or how it went. You do not know, and a client can tell.
5. Do not guilt them. Not 'we haven't seen you in a while', not 'where have you been', not 'we miss you'. Say something warm and forward-looking that gives them an easy way back.
6. If the name above is not really a person's — web forms and mailbox scans leave placeholders like 'Website', 'Contact', 'Info', or an address — do not use it at all.

Return JSON with exactly one field: opening.

steps.name: Send the booking invite
steps.description: `invite_contacts` delegates to `sendBookingLink` with `trigger: 'automated'`, which sends it as MARKETING — so `marketingGate` checks this recipient's own consent at the transport and refuses without it. That check is the one thing in this plan that must never be worked around: the find narrows the list, the gate decides who may actually be written to. SOFT OPT-IN IS DELIBERATELY NOT CLAIMED. The two sibling agents do claim it, and this one must not: the exception covers a message about the same kind of work, sent to somebody whose address came from a recent sale. Six months to eighteen months after the last visit, 'recent' is doing work it cannot bear, and a warm note about coming back is the closest thing in this product to a cold mailshot. This agent reaches only people who said yes.
